title: 🌍 UNIT 5: CHALLENGES OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
notes: Economic development can be hindered by poverty, unequal globalization, regional imbalances, corruption and global health crises.

title: 💰 5.1 MULTIPLE FACES OF POVERTY
notes:
Poverty → a deficiency in the resources and capabilities needed to maintain an acceptable standard of living.

It can involve lack of:
🔹 Income and assets
🔹 Food and shelter
🔹 Safe drinking water
🔹 Education and health care
🔹 Skills, knowledge and opportunities

⭐ Poverty is multidimensional; income alone cannot describe every aspect of deprivation.

title: 📉 5.1.1 ABSOLUTE & RELATIVE POVERTY
notes:
🔴 Absolute poverty → income or resources are insufficient to meet basic necessities such as food, shelter, water, education and health care.

🔵 Relative poverty → people have resources but remain significantly below the average standard of living in their society.

⭐ Absolute = inability to meet basic needs.

⭐ Relative = lower standard of living compared with others.

title: 🧩 5.1.2 DIMENSIONS OF POVERTY
notes:
Poverty can be viewed through several dimensions:

💵 Income → insufficient financial resources.

🍚 Consumption → inadequate access to goods and services.

🎓 Education → limited access to knowledge and skills.

🏥 Health → inadequate health and nutrition.

🏠 Living conditions → poor housing, water and sanitation.

⚖️ Empowerment → limited ability to influence decisions affecting one's life.

⭐ Poverty involves both material deprivation and limited opportunities.

title: 🔍 5.1.3 CAUSES OF POVERTY
notes:
Major causes include:

🔹 Unemployment and low incomes.
🔹 Low productivity.
🔹 Limited access to education and health services.
🔹 Unequal distribution of resources.
🔹 Conflict and political instability.
🔹 Environmental degradation.
🔹 Rapid population growth in resource-constrained areas.
🔹 Weak institutions and poor governance.
🔹 Limited access to markets, infrastructure and technology.

title: ⚔️ 5.1.4 CONFLICT & POVERTY
notes:
Conflict and poverty can reinforce each other.

⚔️ Conflict → destroys infrastructure, livelihoods, markets and productive assets.

📉 Poverty → increases vulnerability and can intensify competition over scarce resources.

🔄 Conflict → displacement → loss of income → reduced investment → deeper poverty.

⭐ Peace, security and effective institutions are important for sustainable poverty reduction.

title: 🌱 5.1.5 POVERTY REDUCTION & DEVELOPMENT
notes:
Reducing poverty requires more than increasing national income.

Important measures →
🔹 Create productive employment.
🔹 Improve education and skills.
🔹 Expand health services.
🔹 Improve infrastructure.
🔹 Increase access to markets and finance.
🔹 Promote social protection.
🔹 Reduce inequality.
🔹 Strengthen governance and institutions.

⭐ Development should expand people's income, opportunities, capabilities and quality of life.

title: 🌐 5.2 GLOBALIZATION
notes:
Globalization → a process through which the world becomes increasingly interconnected through commerce, communication, cultural interaction, politics and education.

🔹 Trade and investment connect economies.
🔹 Multinational corporations operate across countries.
🔹 Information and culture spread rapidly through mass media and communication technology.

⭐ Globalization has accelerated greatly during the last several decades.

title: 💼 5.2.1 GLOBALIZATION & DEVELOPING COUNTRIES
notes:
Globalization affects developing countries mainly through:

💰 Economic and trade processes → increased trade, investment and market integration.

🎓 Education and health → greater international exchange of knowledge, technology and services.

🎭 Culture → increased interaction and spread of ideas, languages, lifestyles and products.

⭐ Global integration can create opportunities while also producing new economic and cultural pressures.

title: ✅ 5.2.2 ADVANTAGES OF GLOBALIZATION
notes:
Major advantages include:

🔹 Expansion of international trade.
🔹 Foreign investment and capital flows.
🔹 Creation of employment opportunities.
🔹 Access to new technologies.
🔹 Larger markets for goods and services.
🔹 Greater exchange of knowledge and skills.
🔹 Increased international cooperation.
🔹 Potential reduction of poverty through economic growth.

⭐ Developing economies can benefit when globalization improves productivity, investment and access to markets.

title: ⚠️ 5.2.3 DISADVANTAGES OF GLOBALIZATION
notes:
Possible disadvantages include:

🔹 Local businesses may struggle against powerful multinational corporations.
🔹 Economic benefits may be distributed unequally.
🔹 Local industries can become dependent on external markets.
🔹 Cultural traditions may be weakened or transformed.
🔹 Economic crises can spread between interconnected countries.
🔹 Developing countries may face strong external economic pressures.

⭐ Globalization can increase both opportunity and inequality.

title: 🏢 5.2.4 MULTINATIONAL CORPORATIONS
notes:
Multinational Corporation (MNC) → a company that operates and invests in more than one country.

🔹 Can provide capital and employment.
🔹 Introduce technology and management skills.
🔹 Connect developing economies to global markets.
🔹 Can increase competition and productivity.

⚠️ Large corporations may also dominate local markets and put pressure on smaller domestic businesses.

title: ⚖️ 5.3 GROWING IMBALANCE BETWEEN REGIONS & COUNTRIES
notes:
Global economic development is unevenly distributed.

🌍 Some countries and regions have high incomes, advanced technology and strong infrastructure.

🌍 Others face low incomes, limited services, weak infrastructure and high poverty.

Major dimensions of imbalance →
🔹 Income and wealth
🔹 Technology
🔹 Employment
🔹 Education
🔹 Health
🔹 Infrastructure
🔹 Access to resources and markets

⭐ Unequal development creates differences in living standards between and within countries.

title: 📊 5.3.1 GLOBAL INEQUALITY
notes:
Global inequality → unequal distribution of income, wealth, opportunities and resources among people, regions and countries.

It can occur:
🔹 Between countries.
🔹 Between regions within a country.
🔹 Between urban and rural populations.
🔹 Between social groups.

⭐ Economic growth does not automatically guarantee equal distribution of its benefits.

title: 🌎 5.3.2 GLOBAL NORTH & GLOBAL SOUTH
notes:
🌐 Global North → generally refers to wealthier and more economically developed countries with higher levels of industrialization and income.

🌍 Global South → generally refers to developing countries, many of which face lower incomes, weaker infrastructure and greater development challenges.

⚠️ These terms describe broad economic and geopolitical patterns rather than strict geographical locations.

title: 📈 5.3.3 CAUSES OF REGIONAL IMBALANCE
notes:
Regional and national inequalities can result from:

🔹 Unequal natural-resource endowment.
🔹 Differences in infrastructure.
🔹 Unequal access to technology.
🔹 Historical patterns of development.
🔹 Differences in education and human capital.
🔹 Unequal investment.
🔹 Political instability and conflict.
🔹 Unequal access to international markets.
🔹 Geographic location and accessibility.

title: 🌱 5.3.4 REDUCING DEVELOPMENT IMBALANCES
notes:
Possible approaches →

🔹 Invest in education and health.
🔹 Improve infrastructure and connectivity.
🔹 Promote productive employment.
🔹 Support less-developed regions.
🔹 Expand access to technology.
🔹 Encourage fair trade and investment.
🔹 Strengthen institutions and governance.
🔹 Improve access to finance and markets.

⭐ Balanced development requires expanding opportunities in disadvantaged regions and groups.

title: 🚫 5.4 CORRUPTION
notes:
Corruption → misuse of entrusted power for private or personal gain.

Common forms include:
🔹 Bribery
🔹 Embezzlement
🔹 Fraud
🔹 Extortion
🔹 Nepotism
🔹 Abuse of public office

⭐ Corruption weakens institutions and diverts resources away from development.

title: 🏛️ 5.4.1 CORRUPTION & DEVELOPMENT
notes:
Corruption can:

🔻 Reduce public resources available for development.
🔻 Increase the cost of projects and services.
🔻 Discourage investment.
🔻 Weaken public institutions.
🔻 Reduce trust in government.
🔻 Increase inequality.
🔻 Distort competition and resource allocation.
🔻 Reduce the quality of public services.

⭐ Corruption can become a major barrier to sustainable economic development.

title: 📊 5.4.2 MEASURING CORRUPTION
notes:
Corruption can be difficult to measure directly because corrupt activities are often hidden.

📌 Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) → measures perceived levels of public-sector corruption across countries.

Higher CPI scores → generally indicate lower perceived corruption.
Lower CPI scores → generally indicate higher perceived corruption.

⭐ Corruption indicators help compare perceived corruption between countries.

title: 🔍 5.4.3 CAUSES OF CORRUPTION
notes:
Major factors can include:

🔹 Weak institutions.
🔹 Lack of transparency.
🔹 Limited accountability.
🔹 Excessive concentration of power.
🔹 Poor enforcement of laws.
🔹 Political instability.
🔹 Low public-sector wages in some contexts.
🔹 Lack of effective oversight.
🔹 Opportunities for officials to abuse public resources.

title: ⚠️ 5.4.4 CONSEQUENCES OF CORRUPTION
notes:
Corruption can lead to:

💰 Economic loss → resources are diverted from productive uses.

🏗️ Poor infrastructure → funds may be wasted or misallocated.

📉 Lower investment → businesses face uncertainty and additional costs.

⚖️ Inequality → benefits may favor powerful groups.

🏥 Poor services → health, education and other public services suffer.

🏛️ Weak governance → public trust and institutional effectiveness decline.

⭐ Corruption can reinforce poverty and inequality.

title: 🛡️ 5.4.5 COMBATING CORRUPTION
notes:
Important measures include:

🔹 Strong and independent institutions.
🔹 Transparent public procurement.
🔹 Effective auditing and oversight.
🔹 Enforcement of anti-corruption laws.
🔹 Public access to information.
🔹 Accountability of public officials.
🔹 Protection for people reporting corruption.
🔹 Civic participation and responsible media.

⭐ Transparency + accountability + effective institutions → reduce opportunities for corruption.

title: 🏥 5.5 GLOBAL HEALTH CRISES
notes:
Global health crisis → a health threat that can spread across countries and seriously affect populations, health systems and economies.

Major examples →
🦠 Pandemics and epidemics
💉 Infectious diseases
🌍 Cross-border health emergencies

⭐ Globalization, international travel, urbanization and population mobility can accelerate the spread of infectious diseases.

title: 🦠 5.5.1 EMERGING & RE-EMERGING DISEASES
notes:
Emerging diseases → diseases that newly appear in a population or rapidly increase in incidence or geographic range.

Re-emerging diseases → diseases that had previously declined but return or increase again.

Examples →
🔹 COVID-19
🔹 Ebola
🔹 Marburg
🔹 Zika
🔹 SARS
🔹 MERS

⭐ Disease emergence is influenced by environmental, biological, social and human factors.

title: 🌍 5.5.2 FACTORS BEHIND GLOBAL HEALTH CRISES
notes:
Major contributing factors include:

🔹 International travel and migration.
🔹 Population growth and urbanization.
🔹 Environmental change.
🔹 Deforestation and ecosystem disturbance.
🔹 Close human-animal interaction.
🔹 Weak health systems.
🔹 Poverty and inadequate sanitation.
🔹 Limited access to health services.
🔹 Increased movement of people and goods.

⭐ Health crises often result from interactions between humans, animals and the environment.

title: 🚑 5.5.3 IMPACTS OF GLOBAL HEALTH CRISES
notes:
Global health crises can cause:

🏥 Pressure on health systems.
💰 Economic losses.
👷 Loss of workers and productivity.
🏫 Disruption of education.
✈️ Restrictions on travel and movement.
🏭 Disruption of production and trade.
🍚 Increased food and livelihood insecurity.
😔 Increased social and psychological stress.

⭐ Health emergencies can become economic and social crises as well.

title: 🛡️ 5.5.4 RESPONDING TO GLOBAL HEALTH CRISES
notes:
Effective responses include:

🔹 Disease surveillance and early detection.
🔹 Rapid testing and diagnosis.
🔹 Vaccination where available.
🔹 Treatment and isolation of cases.
🔹 Contact tracing.
🔹 Public-health education.
🔹 International cooperation.
🔹 Strong health systems.
🔹 Clean water, sanitation and hygiene.
🔹 Scientific research and information sharing.

⭐ Early detection + strong health systems + cooperation reduce the impact of health crises.

title: 🧠 UNIT 5 KEY DIFFERENCES
notes:
🔴 Absolute poverty → inability to meet basic needs.

🔵 Relative poverty → lower standard of living compared with the wider society.

🌐 Globalization → increasing worldwide interconnectedness.

🏢 Multinational corporation → company operating in multiple countries.

⚖️ Global inequality → unequal distribution of income, wealth and opportunities.

🌎 Global North → broadly wealthier developed countries.

🌍 Global South → broadly developing countries.

🚫 Corruption → misuse of entrusted power for private gain.\nn📊 CPI → indicator based on perceptions of public-sector corruption.

🦠 Emerging disease → newly appearing/increasing disease.

🔄 Re-emerging disease → previously declining disease that returns or increases.

title: ⭐ UNIT 5 QUICK REVISION
notes:
💰 Poverty → deprivation of resources, capabilities and opportunities.

📉 Two major forms → absolute + relative poverty.

⚔️ Conflict ↔ poverty → each can reinforce the other.

🌐 Globalization → economic + political + educational + cultural interconnectedness.

✅ Benefits → trade + investment + technology + employment + larger markets.

⚠️ Risks → inequality + local-business pressure + cultural change + economic dependence.

⚖️ Global imbalance → unequal income + technology + infrastructure + opportunities.

🚫 Corruption → misuse of entrusted power for personal gain.

📉 Effects → lower investment + wasted resources + weak services + inequality.

🛡️ Anti-corruption → transparency + accountability + strong institutions.

🏥 Global health crises → diseases and health emergencies crossing borders.

🦠 Examples → COVID-19 + Ebola + Marburg + Zika + SARS + MERS.

🌍 Key response → surveillance + prevention + treatment + research + international cooperation.
